sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2006. Change Request Number 2006-057: split [mzf] Aiku into Yangum Mon, Yangum Dey, Yangum Gel, Ambrak (submitted by John Brownie, SIL; supporter Hilkka Arminen). Dallas: SIL International.

Sources of information: 'Alphabet Design Workshop report, written by Hilkka Arminen, plus further correspondence with her' -- i.e. an unpublished SIL-PNG ADW report is the only document known to contain phonological/orthographic notes on the Yangum languages.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 767-780. Canberra: ANU.

sources.note: Nothing. Aiku (819) listed in the Palei Family table; the phylum-wide phonology paragraph (p.769: three positions of articulation, usually no voicing contrast, five to eight vowels, high proportion of fricatives; Olo phoneme inventory and phonotactics) makes no statement about stress for any Palei language.
